About Perry Asset Management

A disciplined, research-driven approach to portfolio management — built on macro intelligence, quantitative rigor, and institutional-grade analytics.

Our Approach

Perry Asset Management combines top-down macro regime analysis with bottom-up fundamental and quantitative research. Our investment process begins with a proprietary six-pillar macro framework covering Real Economic Activity, Labor Markets, Inflation, Monetary Policy, Fiscal Policy, and International Dynamics.

Products & Services

Macro Regime Analysis

Real-time economic scorecard and sector rotation signals built on a CFA-based regime classification framework.

Portfolio Construction

Optimized allocation across equities, fixed income, alternatives, and cash — calibrated to current market conditions.

Risk Analytics

Value at Risk, Monte-Carlo stress testing, tracking error analysis, and scenario modeling across VIX and macro regimes.

Quantitative Research

ML models including regression, random forest, gradient boosting, and time-series forecasting for alpha generation.

Thematic Research

Deep dives into emerging investment themes — AI, crypto, energy transition, space — that adapt as opportunities evolve.

Fundamental & Technical Analysis

DCF valuation, ratio analysis, MACD, RSI, momentum indicators, and sector-level profitability and leverage scoring.

Portfolio Optimization — Regime-Conditioned Weights ?

For each regime, solves for optimal weights across your holdings using Markowitz mean-variance optimization (max Sharpe). Compares to your current weights and shows: (1) recommended rotation actions (e.g., "Add 8% Energy, reduce Tech by 12%"), (2) backtest of optimal weights vs. your actual portfolio over the past 3 years, and (3) projected return uplift if you rotate.

Click "Run Optimization & Backtest" to compute regime-optimal weights and validate them against the past.
Method: Markowitz (1952) mean-variance optimization on per-state expected returns • Solved via gradient projection on long-only simplex (sum to 1, weights ≥ 0) • Regime-conditioned drifts from SPY 5-year history segmented by Perry 4-state classifier • Per-holding beta scaled to SPY proxy • Backtest: holds optimal weights through specified window, compares cumulative return to actual portfolio (equal-weight rebalanced)
Period Returns & Tracking ?

Time-weighted returns reconstructed from the dollar-value series, with active return vs. SPY (broad benchmark) and QQQ (tech-heavy benchmark). Tracking error annualized from daily active-return volatility.

Computing period returns…
Method: Time-weighted return per CFA Institute GIPS standards. Tracking Error = std(Rp − Rb) × √252. Information Ratio = (Rp − Rb) / TE.
Rolling 90-Day Active Return vs. SPY ?
Brinson-Fachler Attribution by Sector ?

Active return decomposed into Allocation (sector tilt vs. SPY), Selection (security picks within sectors), and Interaction (cross-effect). Sector benchmark proxies are SPDR sector ETFs. The model is the Brinson-Fachler (1985) framework — the institutional standard adopted by FactSet Portfolio Analysis and Bloomberg PORT.

Intrinsic Value Estimate — Multi-Method Valuation ?

Three valuation methods run simultaneously: Forward P/E (analyst consensus × sector multiple), Simplified DCF (free cash flow discounted at the 10Y Treasury + risk premium), and Dividend Discount (Gordon Growth, dividend-paying stocks only). Each produces an implied fair value; the consensus band shows where they agree.

Computing intrinsic value...

Macro Regime Analysis

CFA-based macro regime scoring across 6 pillars using real-time Federal Reserve data. All indicators in one unified dashboard.

How this relates to the Portfolio State on Cross-Asset Analysis:
The Macro Regime Verdict here (Early / Mid / Late Cycle / Contraction) uses FRED economic data and operates on a 3–12 month economic cycle frequency. The Portfolio State on Cross-Asset Analysis (Leveraged / Growth / Neutral / Drawdown) uses market price action (VIX, SPY momentum) and operates on a shorter tactical frequency. A "Mid-Cycle" economy can simultaneously produce a "Positioned for Drawdown" portfolio signal when equity valuations are stretched — markets lead the economy by 6–12 months on average. Use the Macro Regime for strategic sector rotation and the Portfolio State for tactical position sizing.

Walk-Forward Backtest (Out-of-Sample Validation) ?

Tests the MLR model's out-of-sample performance by training on an expanding window and testing on the next period, repeatedly. Standard backtests suffer from in-sample overfitting — a model that looks great when evaluated on the data it was trained on may perform poorly on new data. Walk-forward estimates realistic forward performance by never testing on data the model has seen.

Enter a ticker and click "Run Walk-Forward Test" to see out-of-sample predictive performance.
Method: Expanding-window walk-forward validation (White 2000, Pesaran & Timmermann 1995) • Features: 21-day momentum, 63-day volatility, 10-day mean reversion, trailing return, VIX level, beta, RSI14 proxy • OLS regression trained on history up to each fold boundary • Strategy rule: enter long when model's predicted 21-day return exceeds threshold, hold for prediction horizon, exit • Compared against buy-and-hold baseline • No look-ahead bias — every prediction uses only data available at that point in time.

Decision Compass — Where Should Capital Be?

Aggregates macro regime, market breadth, credit signals, and volatility into a single recommended portfolio posture. Each pillar is independently scored and combined into a navy / blue / gray heat map.

Computing posture...
Methodology: Weighted composite of 7 signal pillars — Business Cycle (FRED scorecard, 25%), Market Regime State (VIX/momentum quarterly-locked, 70% flip threshold, 20%), Breadth/Fear-Greed (15%), Credit Conditions (HY OAS + credit spreads, 12%), Yield Curve (8%), Cross-Asset Momentum (10%), Sector Rotation + Cross-Asset Regime Composite (10%; blends sector leadership with 11-pair intermarket regime score when loaded). Perry State acts as a ceiling/floor gate on the final composite. Phase changes require 2 consecutive FRED fetch cycles to commit. Academic grounding: Horvath et al. (2021), Cain (2023), Lyu et al. (2023), Molero-González et al. (2024).

Current Market Regime & Recommended Portfolio State
Why might this differ from the Macro Regime Analysis page?
The Portfolio State here (Leveraged / Growth / Neutral / Drawdown) is a market-timing signal driven by VIX level, SPY distance from its 52-week high, and short-term price momentum. It answers: "What posture should my portfolio take right now based on current market conditions?"
The Macro Regime Verdict on the Macro page (Early / Mid / Late Cycle / Contraction) is a business cycle classification driven by FRED economic indicators (yield curve, unemployment, leading indicators, etc.). It answers: "Where are we in the economic cycle?"
These frameworks operate at different frequencies and measure different things. A "Mid-Cycle" economy can still produce a "Positioned for Drawdown" portfolio signal if equity valuations are stretched and volatility is spiking — the market often leads the economy. Both signals are shown below; use them together.
Analyzing current market state...
Framework: Perry Asset Management 4-state portfolio regime classifier · Inputs: VIX (CBOE), SPY / QQQ price data via Cloudflare Worker, trailing 12-month return, distance-from-52W-high, drawdown-from-peak, Fibonacci retracements.
The Four Portfolio States — Framework Reference ?
Approach: State-based allocation informed by mean-reversion at extremes (Lo 2004), contrarian entry at VIX > 30 (Whaley 2009), Fibonacci retracement cycles (Frost & Prechter, Elliott Wave Principle), and defensive positioning when trailing returns compress forward expected returns (Shiller CAPE).
QQQ Daily Chart with Fibonacci Projections ?

Auto-detects the most recent significant swing low and swing high on QQQ, then plots Fibonacci retracement levels (23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, 78.6%) and projection levels (127.2%, 161.8%, 261.8%). Use these as price pivots — QQQ approaching a key level during a rip is a signal that "Positioned for Drawdown" posture may be appropriate.

Loading QQQ data...
Sources: QQQ price data via Cloudflare Worker / Yahoo Finance · Fibonacci ratios from the golden ratio φ = 1.618 (Frost & Prechter, Elliott Wave Principle) · Swing detection via local-extremum algorithm.
Bayesian Regime Transition Probabilities ?

Given the current classified market state, this estimates the probability of transitioning to each of the four portfolio states over the next 30, 60, and 90 days. Transition matrix is fit from historical SPY regime sequences (5 years of daily data). Use this for position sizing: if P(Drawdown in 60 days) is high, hold more cash even if currently in Growth state.

Uses 5-year historical SPY regime sequence + current classification.
Click "Compute Transition Probabilities" to estimate regime transitions from current state.
Method: Empirical transition matrix P[i,j] = P(state_{t+k} = j | state_t = i) estimated via maximum likelihood from historical 5-year SPY regime sequence • 30/60/90-day transition probabilities computed as P^k where k = horizon/segment length • Bayesian updating: current-state prior combined with transition matrix to produce posterior distribution over future states • Framework: Hamilton (1989) Markov regime-switching, adapted for macro regime classification.
Market Breadth & Composite Fear/Greed Indicator ?

Composite index (0=Extreme Fear, 100=Extreme Greed) built from 7 independently-normalized signals. Each signal contributes equally. Score < 25 = historically bullish contrarian setup; Score > 75 = elevated complacency / risk of correction.

Click Compute to run composite indicator.
Methodology: Each signal normalized to [0,100] via min-max over trailing 252 trading days. Equal-weight composite. Signals: VIX level, VIX/SMA20 ratio, SPY vs. 52W high, TLT/SPY 20D relative return (safe haven), GLD/SPY 20D relative return, HYG/LQD 20D relative return (credit risk appetite), QQQ/SPY 20D relative return (risk appetite). Inspired by CNN Fear & Greed Index; all computations use live market data.
Sector Momentum Scorecard ?

All 11 GICS sector SPDR ETFs ranked by return momentum across multiple time horizons. Composite rank = average of 1M, 3M, 6M, 12M ranks. Top 3 sectors = momentum leaders (typically outperform in the near term). Bottom 3 = candidates for mean-reversion or rotation.

11 GICS sectors via SPDR ETFs (XLK, XLE, XLF, etc.)

Sources: SPDR Select Sector ETFs (State Street). Method: Total return for each period. Composite rank = (rank_1M + rank_3M + rank_6M + rank_12M) / 4 where rank 1 = best. Jegadeesh, N. & Titman, S. (1993) "Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers," Journal of Finance.

Intermarket Lead/Lag Analysis ?

Cross-correlation function (CCF) between selected pairs at lags −20 to +20 trading days. Positive peak at lag k means the leader's return today correlates with the follower's return k days later. Classic relationships: Copper leads Equities, Rates lead Credit, Oil leads Energy stocks.

Select assets and click Compute Lead/Lag.
Method: Cross-correlation function r_AB(k) = corr(R_A(t), R_B(t+k)) for k ∈ [-20, +20]. Computed from daily log returns. Bonferroni-corrected 95% confidence band = ±1.96/√n shown as dashed lines. Granger, C.W.J. (1969) "Investigating Causal Relations by Econometric Models," Econometrica.
Market Breadth: Is the Rally Broadening? ?

Equal-weight vs. cap-weight S&P 500 (RSP ÷ SPY ratio) is the cleanest single measure of market breadth. Rising ratio = participation expanding, broad-based leadership. Falling ratio = mega-cap concentration increasing, narrowing breadth — historically a late-cycle vulnerability signal.

Also shown: IWM vs. SPY (Small Cap vs. Large Cap) — small caps outperform when domestic growth expectations are strong and financial conditions are easing. Both signals are consistent with the Quantamental framework (Cain 2023): technical breadth confirming or diverging from fundamental cycle positioning.

RSP/SPY & IWM/SPY with 63D SMA — monthly regime frequency
Click Load Broadening Charts to compute.
Framework: Horvath, B., Issa, A. & Muguruza, A. (2021) "Clustering Market Regimes using the Wasserstein Distance." Breadth divergence between RSP and SPY reflects distributional shift in cross-asset return patterns — a precursor to regime transitions. Cain, C. (2023) "Quantementals." Price data via Cloudflare Worker / Yahoo Finance.
Where Is Liquidity Moving? — 11-Sector Flow Scorecard ?

Capital rotation across GICS sectors as a real-time proxy for where institutional liquidity is flowing. Each sector is scored on 1M and 3M price momentum relative to SPY, then bucketed into Inflow, Neutral, or Outflow. The composite rotation vector identifies the dominant narrative (e.g., "defensive rotation into staples/utilities," "reflation into energy/materials," "growth into tech").

11 SPDR ETFs · 1M + 3M relative to SPY
Method: 1M and 3M excess return vs. SPY. Score = 0.4×(1M rank) + 0.6×(3M rank). Inflow: top 4 sectors. Outflow: bottom 4. Neutral: middle 3. Rotation narrative generated from sector groupings. Sources: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993); Cain, C. (2023) "Quantementals — Combining Technical and Fundamental Analysis." Price data via Cloudflare Worker / Yahoo Finance.
8 · Cross-Asset Regime Signals ?

Eleven intermarket ratios with 63-day SMA overlay (monthly frequency — filters daily noise). Green shading = ratio above SMA (Risk-On); red shading = below (Risk-Off). Composite regime score computed from all 11 pairs, with RSP/SPY and IWM/SPY weighted 2× as primary breadth indicators. Composite feeds into the Master Verdict Pillar 7 when loaded. SMA upgraded from 20D to 63D per Horvath et al. (2021): short-window signals are regime-unstable; distributional shifts in cross-asset relationships require monthly-frequency confirmation. RMT insight (Molero-González et al. 2024): dominant eigenvalue concentration in the correlation matrix accompanies the XLK/RSP ratio rising — both signal narrowing breadth and increased systemic fragility.

Loads independently of universe selection.
Sources & Academic Grounding: Murphy, J.J. (1991) Intermarket Analysis, John Wiley & Sons · CFA Institute Business Cycle framework (L1-L3) · Horvath, B., Issa, A. & Muguruza, A. Quantamental Composite — Technical × Fundamental Signal Fusion ?

Per Cain (2023): fundamental analysis identifies what should happen; technical analysis identifies when it is happening. The Quantamental framework multiplies these signals — only acting with high conviction when both agree. A fundamentally strong sector with weak price momentum may be early-cycle value; a technically strong sector with weak fundamentals may be in a momentum regime with risk of sharp reversal.

Requires FRED macro data (load Macro page first) + sector momentum
Framework: Cain, C. (2023) "Quantementals: Combining Technical and Fundamental Analysis in a Quantitative Framework for Better Investment Results." Signal = F_score × T_score where F_score ∈ [-1,+1] from FRED pillar scores and T_score ∈ [-1,+1] from 1M–3M price momentum vs. SPY. Quadrant classification: Quant-Confirm (both +), Fundamental-Led (F+ / T-), Technical-Led (F- / T+), Quant-Avoid (both -). · Sector ETF price data via Cloudflare Worker / Yahoo Finance.
Omega-Ratio Regime-Conditioned Rebalancing Signal ?

The Omega ratio Ω(τ) = E[max(R−τ,0)] / E[max(τ−R,0)] measures full-distribution risk-adjusted return above a threshold τ. Ω > 1 means expected upside above τ exceeds expected downside below τ. Combined with the Perry regime state, this signals when rebalancing toward or away from risk assets is supported by the full return distribution — not just mean/variance. Particularly useful for validating tactical tilts suggested by the Master Verdict.

SPY, TLT, GLD, IWM, QQQ, HYG · 63-day rolling
Framework: Lyu, B. et al. (2023) "Omega: Robust Online Portfolio Optimization with Cash Flows." Ω(τ) = ∫_τ^∞(1−F(r))dr / ∫_{−∞}^τ F(r)dr computed from empirical return distribution (63-day rolling). τ = daily return threshold. Ω > 1.5 = strong upside skew (add exposure); Ω < 0.8 = downside risk dominant (reduce exposure). Regime-conditioned: threshold adjusted by 0.5× in Drawdown regime (more conservative) and 1.5× in Leveraged regime (more aggressive upside expected). · Price data via Cloudflare Worker / Yahoo Finance.

Risk-On / Risk-Off Regime Classification ?
Method: Rule-based classifier using 20D and 63D returns of SPY, TLT, GLD, UUP, USO. Risk-On: SPY > TLT & SPY > GLD. Risk-Off: TLT > SPY & GLD rising. Reflation: USO+XLE lead, SPY positive. Stagflation: commodities up, SPY & TLT both down.

Cross-Asset Regime Distance & RMT Correlation Analysis ?

Wasserstein-1 distance (Horvath et al. 2021) between rolling return distributions and stylized historical regimes. Unlike Frobenius distance on correlations, Wasserstein measures the full distributional shift — capturing changes in tail behavior, skewness, and kurtosis that correlation matrices miss. Also computes RMT Informative Content Ratio (Molero-González et al. 2024): fraction of eigenvalue variance above the Marchenko-Pastur noise ceiling — a direct measure of how much genuine cross-asset structure exists vs. random noise.

Click Compute Regime Distance + RMT to run analysis.
Methods: Wasserstein-1: W₁(P,Q) = ∫|F_P(x) − F_Q(x)|dx — earth-mover distance between empirical CDFs of rolling returns. Measures distributional shift, not just correlation structure. Horvath, B., Issa, A. & Muguruza, A. (2021) "Clustering Market Regimes using the Wasserstein Distance." · Frobenius: ‖C_t − C_ref‖_F shown for comparison. · RMT / Marchenko-Pastur: λ_max = σ²(1 + 1/√q)² where q = T/N. Eigenvalues above λ_max are informative; below are noise. ICR = Σ(λ_i − λ̄_noise)·1[λ_i > λ_max] / Σλ_i. Molero-González, L. et al. (2024) "The random matrix-based informative content of correlation matrices in stock markets." · Universe: SPY, TLT, GLD, UUP, USO, HYG. Price data via Cloudflare Worker / Yahoo Finance.
